audit_status.source_base: Greek James text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact draft reviewed for rich oppressors, laborers' wages, patience, oaths, prayer, anointing, restoration.

verses.restored: Come now, rich ones, weep, howling over your hardships coming upon you.

familiar.text: Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you.

modern.text: Come now, you who are rich, weep and wail over the misery to come upon you.

original.text: Ἄγε νῦν οἱ πλούσιοι, κλαύσατε ὀλολύζοντες ἐπὶ ταῖς ταλαιπωρίαις ὑμῶν ταῖς ἐπερχομέναις.

verses.restored: Your wealth has rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten.

familiar.text: Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are motheaten.

modern.text: Your riches have rotted and moths have eaten your clothes.

original.text: ὁ πλοῦτος ὑμῶν σέσηπεν, καὶ τὰ ἱμάτια ὑμῶν σητόβρωτα γέγονεν,

verses.restored: Your gold and silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be witness against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You stored treasure in last days.

familiar.text: Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.

modern.text: Your gold and silver are corroded. Their corrosion will testify against you and consume your flesh like fire. You have hoarded treasure in the last days.

original.text: ὁ χρυσὸς ὑμῶν καὶ ὁ ἄργυρος κατίωται, καὶ ὁ ἰὸς αὐτῶν εἰς μαρτύριον ὑμῖν ἔσται καὶ φάγεται τὰς σάρκας ὑμῶν· ὡς πῦρ ἐθησαυρίσατε ἐν ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις.

verses.restored: Look, the wage of the workers who harvested your fields, withheld by you, cries out, and the cries of the harvesters have entered the ears of Lord of hosts.

familiar.text: Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of the Lord of sabaoth.

modern.text: Look, the wages you withheld from the workmen who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.

original.text: ἰδοὺ ὁ μισθὸς τῶν ἐργατῶν τῶν ἀμησάντων τὰς χώρας ὑμῶν ὁ ⸀ἀφυστερημένος ἀφʼ ὑμῶν κράζει, καὶ αἱ βοαὶ τῶν θερισάντων εἰς τὰ ὦτα Κυρίου Σαβαὼθ ⸀εἰσεληλύθασιν·

verses.restored: You lived luxuriously upon the earth and indulged yourselves; you nourished your hearts in a day of slaughter.

familiar.text: Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter.

modern.text: You have lived on earth in luxury and self-indulgence. You have fattened your hearts in the day of slaughter.

original.text: ἐτρυφήσατε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐσπαταλήσατε, ἐθρέψατε τὰς καρδίας ⸀ὑμῶν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ σφαγῆς.

verses.restored: You condemned, you murdered the righteous/just one; he does not resist you.

familiar.text: Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you.

modern.text: You have condemned and murdered the righteous, who did not resist you. Patience in Suffering (Job 1:1–5)

original.text: κατεδικάσατε, ἐφονεύσατε τὸν δίκαιον. οὐκ ἀντιτάσσεται ὑμῖν;

verses.restored: Therefore be patient, siblings, until the presence/arrival of the Lord. Look, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it until it receives early and late rain.

familiar.text: Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain.

modern.text: Be patient, then, brothers, until the Lord’s coming. See how the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the soil—how patient he is for the fall and spring rains.

original.text: Μακροθυμήσατε οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ἕως τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ κυρίου. ἰδοὺ ὁ γεωργὸς ἐκδέχεται τὸν τίμιον καρπὸν τῆς γῆς, μακροθυμῶν ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτῷ ἕως ⸀λάβῃ πρόϊμον καὶ ὄψιμον.

verses.restored: You also be patient; establish your hearts, because the presence/arrival of the Lord has drawn near.

familiar.text: Be ye also patient; stablish your hearts: for the coming of the Lord draweth nigh.

modern.text: You, too, be patient and strengthen your hearts, because the Lord’s coming is near.

original.text: μακροθυμήσατε καὶ ὑμεῖς, στηρίξατε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν, ὅτι ἡ παρουσία τοῦ κυρίου ἤγγικεν.

verses.restored: Do not groan against one another, siblings, so that you may not be judged. Look, the Judge stands before the doors.

familiar.text: Grudge not one against another, brethren, lest ye be condemned: behold, the judge standeth before the door.

modern.text: Do not complain about one another, brothers, so that you will not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door!

original.text: μὴ στενάζετε, ⸂ἀδελφοί, κατʼ ἀλλήλων⸃, ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε· ἰδοὺ ὁ κριτὴς πρὸ τῶν θυρῶν ἕστηκεν.

verses.restored: Take, siblings, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord as example of suffering and patience.

familiar.text: Take, my brethren, the prophets, who have spoken in the name of the Lord, for an example of suffering affliction, and of patience.

modern.text: Brothers, as an example of patience in affliction, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

original.text: ὑπόδειγμα λάβετε, ⸀ἀδελφοί, τῆς κακοπαθίας καὶ τῆς μακροθυμίας τοὺς προφήτας, οἳ ἐλάλησαν ⸀ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου.

verses.restored: Look, we call blessed those who endured. You heard of the endurance of Job and saw the Lord's end, that the Lord is deeply compassionate and merciful.

familiar.text: Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.

modern.text: See how blessed we consider those who have persevered. You have heard of Job’s perseverance and have seen the outcome from the Lord. The Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

original.text: ἰδοὺ μακαρίζομεν τοὺς ⸀ὑπομείναντας· τὴν ὑπομονὴν Ἰὼβ ἠκούσατε, καὶ τὸ τέλος κυρίου ⸀εἴδετε, ὅτι πολύσπλαγχνός ἐστιν ⸂ὁ κύριος⸃ καὶ οἰκτίρμων.

verses.restored: But above all, my siblings, do not swear, neither by heaven nor by earth nor by any other oath; but let your yes be yes and your no be no, so that you may not fall under judgment.

familiar.text: But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.

modern.text: Above all, my brothers, do not swear, not by heaven or earth or by any other oath. Simply let your “Yes” be yes, and your “No,” no, so that you will not fall under judgment. The Prayer of Faith

original.text: Πρὸ πάντων δέ, ἀδελφοί μου, μὴ ὀμνύετε, μήτε τὸν οὐρανὸν μήτε τὴν γῆν μήτε ἄλλον τινὰ ὅρκον· ἤτω δὲ ὑμῶν τὸ Ναὶ ναὶ καὶ τὸ Οὒ οὔ, ἵνα μὴ ⸂ὑπὸ κρίσιν⸃ πέσητε.

verses.restored: Is anyone among you suffering? Let one pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let one sing praise.

familiar.text: Is any among you afflicted? let him pray. Is any merry? let him sing psalms.

modern.text: Is any one of you suffering? He should pray. Is anyone cheerful? He should sing praises.

original.text: Κακοπαθεῖ τις ἐν ὑμῖν; προσευχέσθω· εὐθυμεῖ τις; ψαλλέτω.

verses.restored: Is anyone among you weak/sick? Let one call the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over one, anointing with oil in the name of the Lord.

familiar.text: Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord:

modern.text: Is any one of you sick? He should call the elders of the church to pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.

original.text: ἀσθενεῖ τις ἐν ὑμῖν; προσκαλεσάσθω τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους τῆς ἐκκλησίας, καὶ προσευξάσθωσαν ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἀλείψαντες ⸀αὐτὸν ἐλαίῳ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου·

verses.restored: And the prayer of trust will save/heal the weary one, and the Lord will raise one up; and if one has committed sins/misalignments, it will be released/forgiven.

familiar.text: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him.

modern.text: And the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick. The Lord will raise him up. If he has sinned, he will be forgiven.

original.text: καὶ ἡ εὐχὴ τῆς πίστεως σώσει τὸν κάμνοντα, καὶ ἐγερεῖ αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος· κἂν ἁμαρτίας ᾖ πεποιηκώς, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: Therefore confess misalignments to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The active prayer of a righteous/just one is very strong.

familiar.text: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.

modern.text: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail.

original.text: ἐξομολογεῖσθε ⸀οὖν ἀλλήλοις ⸂τὰς ἁμαρτίας⸃ καὶ ⸀εὔχεσθε ὑπὲρ ἀλλήλων, ὅπως ἰαθῆτε. πολὺ ἰσχύει δέησις δικαίου ἐνεργουμένη.

verses.restored: Elijah was a human of like-feeling with us, and he prayed with prayer that it not rain, and it did not rain upon the earth three years and six months.

familiar.text: Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain: and it rained not on the earth by the space of three years and six months.

modern.text: Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years.

original.text: Ἠλίας ἄνθρωπος ἦν ὁμοιοπαθὴς ἡμῖν, καὶ προσευχῇ προσηύξατο τοῦ μὴ βρέξαι, καὶ οὐκ ἔβρεξεν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐνιαυτοὺς τρεῖς καὶ μῆνας ἕξ·

verses.restored: And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth produced its fruit.

familiar.text: And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit.

modern.text: Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth yielded its crops. Restoring a Sinner

original.text: καὶ πάλιν προσηύξατο, καὶ ὁ οὐρανὸς ⸂ὑετὸν ἔδωκεν⸃ καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐβλάστησεν τὸν καρπὸν αὐτῆς.

verses.restored: My siblings, if anyone among you is led astray from the truth and someone turns that one back,

familiar.text: Brethren, if any of you do err from the truth, and one convert him;

modern.text: My brothers, if one of you should wander from the truth and someone should bring him back,

original.text: Ἀδελφοί ⸀μου, ἐάν τις ἐν ὑμῖν πλανηθῇ ἀπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ ἐπιστρέψῃ τις αὐτόν,

verses.restored: let that one know that the one turning back a sinner/misaligned one from wandering way will save/heal that one's soul/life from death and cover a multitude of sins/misalignments.

familiar.text: Let him know, that he which converteth the sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall hide a multitude of sins.

modern.text: consider this: Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover over a multitude of sins.

original.text: ⸀γινωσκέτω ὅτι ὁ ἐπιστρέψας ἁμαρτωλὸν ἐκ πλάνης ὁδοῦ αὐτοῦ σώσει ψυχὴν ⸀αὐτοῦ ἐκ θανάτου καὶ καλύψει πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν.

translation_notes: James 5 targets exploitative wealth, specifically withheld wages and luxury built on harm.
Healing language is prayerful and communal without promising mechanical outcomes.
Job is referenced through endurance and the Lord's compassion/mercy, aligning with the earlier completed Job framework.
